items.item_text: Basic Life Support authorized by the American Heart Association - CPR

Maintains patient safety while transporting patients to and from various departments within the hospital by appropriate means: wheelchair, gurney, bed, or by ambulation. Utilizes lift devices safely and appropriately. The time of transport shall comply with department guidelines 95%-98% of the time as measured by transport logs and record review.
Uses two patient identifiers, in accordance with National Patient Safety Goals, to ensure patient identity 100% of the time.
Transports equipment and specimens to and from various departments within the hospital, responding to calls by delivering requested equipment within 15 minutes at least 90% of the time.
Reports equipment issues to supervisor or seeks appropriate resources for repairs within one hour 96%-98% of the time.

Informs department staff immediately of any patient status changes and delays and notifies the care team members whenever a patient leaves or returns to the nursing unit. Measured by observation and no more than 1-3 formal complaints per year.

Records each patient transport accurately on the nursing unit each time a patient is transported; observes all patient precautions identified at the bedside. Measured by no more than 1-3 formal omissions per year.
